output.methodChoice: Collected X10 first (per-cell timing, which separates the staggered gateway rollout from the fleet config push and includes a no-push control cell and a gateway-rollback test), then X3 (storage-node metrics for the mechanism and the backlog history). Stopped at 2 items.
output.brief:
Don't roll back the gateway. The latency jump comes from the storage team's compaction change (FC-7710), pushed to eleven of twelve cells between 23:38 and 23:52 on 2 Nov, not from gateway 5.8. Config pushes aren't on the shared calendar, so only the gateway looked like a suspect.

Why I'm confident: in each cell that got the push, latency crossed 150 ms within minutes, including eu-w cells that didn't get 5.8 for hours. The one cell that got 5.8 but skipped the push (aps-3) stayed near 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. On the storage nodes, compaction threads rose from 2 to 6, disks hit 97% busy and read queue wait rose about 200 ms, matching the added latency. The network fault began later, in one region.

Rollback would also reopen the signature-replay weakness and leave the real problem.

Next: revert the compaction change in one cell, watching p99 and backlog (4.0% now; at 2 threads it shouldn't reach 15% before 13 Nov), then extend. Don't pause compaction. Hold off throttling Orrin until the 10 Nov attribution. Confidence: high on cause, moderate on what drove the backlog.
